In rare cases, it may be necessary for employees to bring their children to the worksite during regular work hours for short periods of time. In such instances, this period of time should not exceed one (1) hour.
p
A. Circumstances which may warrant the presence of children at the workplace during regular work hours may include, but may not be limited to:
p
1. A breakdown of child care arrangements,
p
2. Before or after scheduled doctor appointments, or
p
3. Brief visitation of parent’s workplace and to meet coworkers.
p
B. When circumstances might warrant the presence of children in the workplace, the following guidelines should be followed:
p
1. Prior approval must be obtained from the supervisor.
p
2. Children must be escorted and supervised at all times.
p

3. For safety reasons, children shall be prohibited from having access to office equipment (e.g., shredders, paper cutters, printers, copiers, etc.), fitness equipment (unless part of a departmentally-approved and supervised youth program or activity), hazardous material areas, areas requiring security clearance, and areas requiring specific safety training, equipment or clothing.
p
4. Children will not be permitted in public service areas, field, or patrol operations.
p
5. Children will not be permitted to ride in city vehicles.
p
6. Employees are responsible for the actions of their children. If the child is disruptive, the employee will be asked to take the child out of the workplace.
p
7. Children with contagious, or potentially contagious, illnesses are not allowed at the workplace.
p
C. A Deputy Chief, Assistant Director, or their designee may set additional guidelines to conform with the operations at a particular location or facility.
p

D. Upon approval, a Deputy Chief, Assistant Director, or their designee may permit employees to participate in “Take Your Child to Work” day events and may limit or prohibit such events at specific sites or facilities.
p

E. Permission to bring a child to work is a privilege, not a right or entitlement. Deputy Chiefs, Assistant Directors, or their designees shall make decisions in the best interest of the organization regarding bringing children into a workplace and these decisions are final.
